We instantiate a five-entry catalogue $\{\kappa_i\}_{i=1}^{5}$ that exercises every adapter in our prototype: two Postgres templates (schema-scoped \textsc{update}/\textsc{delete} and \textsc{create}/\textsc{drop}~\textsc{table}), a Git \textsc{force-push} guard for non-protected refs, and two cloud templates covering SSM parameter writes and RDS snapshot lifecycle. Each $\kappa$ pairs a workload-specific compensator (snapshot restore, migration replay, reflog replay, prior-version restore, point-in-time restore) with a payout schedule calibrated to the loss codes that template can produce; bonds are sized at $10\times$ the per-claim cap so $E_{\text{open}}+P_{\max}$ stays inside $\maxAggregateExposure$ (cf.~main.tex:225). All five register against a deployed \textsc{RecourseRegistry} on an Anvil instance (chain id $31337$) with mean cost 552711\,gas (range 552711--552711), demonstrating that the on-chain admission path is workload-agnostic.
